data.gender_notes: Shahabaz is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Shahabaz is derived from Persian and Arabic origins. It is composed of two words: Shah, meaning king or lord, and Bahaz, meaning world. The name thus translates to 'Lord of the World' or 'Ruler of the Universe'. The name Shahabaz carries the meaning “Lord of the World” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Hindi, Urdu. Parents who choose Shahabaz usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the world and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Shahabaz is a powerful name that embodies leadership, strength, and the ability to rule over one's domain. It is a name that inspires confidence and respect, and is often given to boys who are destined for greatness.
data.etymology: Shahabaz belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the World.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Shahabaz total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

historical_references.reference: Shahabaz Khan was a notable Mughal commander and a close confidant of Emperor Shah Jahan. He was a Persian nobleman, and played a key role in the Battle of Samugarh in 1661, where the Mughal forces defeated the Maratha confederacy led by Shivaji Bhonsle.

Shahabaz Khan also served as the Subahdar (Governor) of Bengal during the reign of Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb in the late 17th century. During his tenure, he expanded the Mughal territories in Bengal and Bihar, and established the city of Murshidabad as the capital of Bengal Subah.
